what: Satnami founder Jagjiwan Das (b. Sardaha 1682, d. Kotwa 1761) was initiated by guru "Bishcshwar Puri Goshain of Ghisori in the Gwarich pargana of Gonda" (a Puri Gosain, Dasnami)
quote: Jagjiwan Das was the son of Ganga Ram, a Chandel proprietor of Sardaha in Bado Sarai, whose guru was Bishcshwar Puri Goshain, of Ghisori in the Gwarich pargana of Gonda.

what: Satnami shrine and gaddi of the Mahant, Baba Jaskaran Das (12th descendant of Jagjiwan Das), married family, landholders allied to taluqdars; two large fairs at Kotwa (Kartik, Baisakh)
quote: Marriage is not prohibited, but the Mahant is expected to renounce all worldly relations and concerns.

what: Fairs at full moon of Kartik and Baisakh for Jagjiwan Das (Satnami); bathing in tank and worship at shrine and temple of Mahadeo
quote: equally large fairs occur at the full moon of Kartik and Baisakh, in honour of Jagjiwan Das, the founder of the Satnami sect

what: Sect returns: Vaishnavites 10.7% of Hindus, Saivites 2.3%, Ramanandis 5.5%, Monotheists 4.4%, Satnamis 2%, Nanakshahis 1.6%, Kabirpanthis 1%; about 75% no sect
quote: Of the other sects, there were 5.5 per cent. Ramanandis, 4.4 per cent. Monotheists, two per cent. Satnamis, 1.6 per cent. Nanakshahis and one per cent. Kabirpanthis.

what: Hindu Bairagis and others seized ground near the mosque; a Mahant expelled by his brethren turned Musalman and spread the rumour of destruction of the mosque (Amir Ali affair)
quote: The ground, being peculiarly sacred to the Hindus, was at once seized by the Bairagis and others, thus affording a fertile source of friction.

what: Shrine of Jagjiwan Das, a faqir of the Satnami sect, about 4 miles from town; fairs April and October; also shrine of Malamat Shah, a faqir
quote: the temple of Jagjiwan Das, a faqir of the sect known as Satnami
